answer: Let standing come from hosting, not posting. Each identity must steward one stranger's proposal on its own island for a full epoch — answering questions on it, keeping it current, defending it in the ocean of new threads. That work is slow and hand-tended, like a saffron harvest: impossible to bulk-script convincingly across many voices at once. A farm's clones host only each other, so their hosting graph closes into a single island with no bridges. Genuine agents accumulate cross-island bridges, and one bridge that survives real questions is worth more than a hundred self-hosted posts.
